quickAnswer: Foreign CTOs and engineering leaders evaluating tech outsourcing in Türkiye focus on four flagship hubs: İTÜ ARI Teknokent, Yıldız Teknopark, and Teknopark İstanbul in Istanbul, plus ODTÜ Teknokent in Ankara. Türkiye offers permanent UTC+3 overlap with Europe, senior engineering rates 25–35% below Eastern Europe, and statutory R&D tax incentives through December 31, 2028.

body.text: Where are Istanbul's main Teknoparks (İTÜ Arı, Yıldız, Teknopark Istanbul) and Ankara's ODTÜ Teknokent?

Istanbul's three core hubs sit across distinct corridors: İTÜ ARI Teknokent in Maslak on the European business spine, Yıldız Teknopark at Davutpaşa in Esenler, and Teknopark İstanbul in Pendik next to Sabiha Gökçen Airport. Ankara's flagship ODTÜ Teknokent occupies the Middle East Technical University campus in Çankaya, anchoring deep-tech, defense, and enterprise R&D.

Each campus attracts a different talent profile and industry cluster. [İTÜ ARI Teknokent](https://www.ariteknokent.com.tr/en) draws fintech, SaaS, and AI scale-ups close to Levent and Maslak financial towers. [YTÜ Yıldız Teknopark](https://www.yildizteknopark.com.tr/en) hosts over 14,000 active R&D personnel across e-commerce, industrial software, and gaming. On the Asian side, [Teknopark İstanbul](https://www.teknoparkistanbul.com.tr/en) specializes in aerospace, maritime, cybersecurity, and embedded engineering, while [ODTÜ Teknokent](https://odtuteknokent.com.tr/en/) leads Türkiye's university-backed deep-tech and systems engineering ecosystem.
How do engineering rates, UTC+3 time zone and English fluency compare to Eastern Europe?

In 2026, senior Turkish software engineers typically bill €35–€60 per hour compared with €50–€80 in Poland, Romania, and Ukraine, cutting six-month team costs by roughly 25–35%. Türkiye operates permanently on UTC+3, giving full-day overlap with London, Frankfurt, and Dubai, while graduates from English-medium universities like ODTÜ, İTÜ, Boğaziçi, and Bilkent maintain strong technical English.

Recent 2026 nearshore rate benchmarks from [Makrops](https://makrops.com/en/blog/en-iyi-yazilim-firmalari-2026-turkiye-avrupa-global) and [Melexsoft](https://www.melexsoft.com/blog/nearshoring-turkey-2026) place Turkish blended product-team costs 40–60% below Western European hubs such as Germany and the Netherlands. Because Türkiye does not observe daylight saving time, sprint ceremonies with UK and DACH teams stay predictable with just a one- to three-hour shift. Technical documentation and pull-request communication are strongest among teams recruiting from Ankara and Istanbul's top engineering faculties; vetting actual squad leads—rather than only sales directors—remains essential during site visits.
What R&D tax incentives exist for foreign tech subsidiaries?

Under Türkiye's Technology Development Zones regime (Law No. 4691), qualifying software and R&D profits earned inside a Teknopark are exempt from corporate tax and application-software VAT through December 31, 2028. Eligible R&D wages receive income tax relief and 50% employer social security support, while Law No. 7582 expands service-export deductions outside zones.

Per [Invest in Türkiye's Investment Zones guide](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/investment-zones.aspx), companies operating approved projects inside a Teknopark also benefit from customs duty and stamp duty exemptions on R&D-related imports and documents. In addition, [Law No. 7582](https://www.legal500.com/intelligence/turkey/tax/law-no-7582-on-the-amendment-of-certain-laws-published-in-the-official-gazette-dated-4-june-2026) (published June 4, 2026) expanded service-export deductions for qualifying software and IT firms billing foreign clients.

How do you structure a 3-day vendor evaluation trip?

An efficient three-day evaluation splits Istanbul by continent to avoid Bosphorus bridge bottlenecks before taking an early morning flight to Ankara. Dedicate Day 1 to European-side vendors at İTÜ ARI and Yıldız Teknopark, Day 2 to Teknopark İstanbul near Sabiha Gökçen, and Day 3 to ODTÜ Teknokent plus independent legal and CPA briefings.
Follow this operational checklist to keep technical due diligence sharp:

items: Day 1 (Istanbul European Side): Base in Maslak or Levent; schedule two 90-minute technical deep dives at İTÜ ARI Teknokent and one afternoon audit at Yıldız Teknopark.
Day 2 (Istanbul Asian Side): Cross early to Teknopark İstanbul in Pendik for embedded or enterprise vendor reviews; depart from adjacent SAW airport to Ankara (ESB) in the evening.
Day 3 (Ankara): Meet shortlisted ODTÜ Teknokent engineering leads in the morning, followed by an independent Turkish SMMM and corporate attorney session on IP and Law No. 4691 rules.
Technical verification: Request live architecture walkthroughs with the actual engineers assigned to your account, not pre-sales managers.

faq.q: Can a 100% foreign-owned company open an office inside a Turkish Teknopark?
faq.a: Yes. Foreign investors may incorporate a 100% foreign-owned Turkish LLC or Joint Stock Company and apply to a Technology Development Zone management board with an approved R&D or software project.

faq.q: Until when are Türkiye's Law No. 4691 Teknopark tax exemptions currently valid?
faq.a: According to Invest in Türkiye, the core corporate tax, VAT, and R&D personnel tax exemptions inside Technology Development Zones currently run through December 31, 2028.

faq.q: How long does travel between Istanbul and Ankara take during a vendor evaluation trip?
faq.a: Direct flights between Istanbul (IST or SAW) and Ankara Esenboğa (ESB) take roughly 65 minutes, while the YHT high-speed train from Söğütlüçeşme to Ankara takes about 4.5 hours.

faq.q: Which Istanbul Teknopark is closest to Sabiha Gökçen Airport?
faq.a: Teknopark İstanbul in Pendik sits directly adjacent to Sabiha Gökçen International Airport (SAW) on the Asian side, making single-day fly-in visits straightforward.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye incorporate tech subsidiaries or file tax incentive applications?
faq.a: No. We plan your itinerary, Teknopark meetings, and introductions to independent lawyers and SMMMs (CPAs), who handle incorporation, Law No. 4691 filings, and tax compliance.

faq.q: What is the time difference between Türkiye and Central European Time?
faq.a: Türkiye stays on permanent UTC+3 year-round, placing it two hours ahead of Central European Time (CET) in winter and one hour ahead of Central European Summer Time (CEST).
